title: Protecting the P-Trap Seal from Siphonage
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. Siphonage occurs when a trap arm lacks proper venting or drops too low before reaching the vent connection, creating a siphon vacuum that pulls water out of the trap seal. To preserve this vital water barrier, always ensure the trap arm maintains proper slope without dropping below the trap weir elevation before connecting to the vent. Never double-trap a fixture, as trapped air pockets cause sluggish drainage and seal displacement.

Protecting the P-Trap Seal from Siphonage

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. Siphonage occurs when a trap arm lacks proper venting or drops too low before reaching the vent connection, creating a siphon vacuum that pulls water out of the trap seal. To preserve this vital water barrier, always ensure the trap arm maintains proper slope without dropping below the trap weir elevation before connecting to the vent. Never double-trap a fixture, as trapped air pockets cause sluggish drainage and seal displacement.
